clue.text: Independent journalist, say, more at liberty to include something cutting?

indicators.note: to include means the comparative word holds the cutting thing within it

parts.note: more at liberty is freer
a lance is a blade used for cutting, as a surgeon's lancet

explanation.surface: A newspaper writer working independently is freer and might carry a sharp weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to include' puts LANCE inside FREER, after its FREE. 'Independent' doubles as a nod to the newspaper itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-employed writer selling work to many papers is the classic example of an independent journalist.

clue.text: Get on with companions going on a cruise

definitions.text: Get on with companions going on a cruise

parts.words: Get on with companions going on a cruise
parts.note: the picture is of boarding a ship with friends at the start of a voyage; 'get on' is also to go aboard

explanation.definitionFit: To go aboard a ship at the start of a voyage is the sense, and 'get on' is a plain synonym of boarding.

clue.text: Egg-producer, aptly, sorted out the matter

indicators.note: sorted out means the letters of aptly are put into a new order

parts.note: pus is the matter that collects in an infected wound

explanation.surface: Something that lays eggs has neatly dealt with the issue at hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorted out' rearranges APTLY to PLATY; PUS is 'the matter' in the medical sense of discharge.
explanation.definitionFit: The duck-billed mammal of Australia is famous as one of the few mammals that lay eggs.

clue.text: Importance of old-fashioned scruples, say

explanation.definitionFit: Importance is significance or heft in an argument; scruples were old apothecaries' units of mass, examples of measures of heaviness.

clue.text: Business built around pilot schemes

parts.note: pilot schemes sound like trial projects, but here they are schemes run by people who fly planes, an industry of flight

explanation.definitionFit: The industry of flying aircraft is literally organised around airline pilots and their flights.

clue.text: Tail of Lepus, short

indicators.note: tail of asks for the final letter of the word Lepus

parts.note: cut, as in a film cut short or a cut-down version

explanation.surface: The hare constellation's tail is a stubby one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tail of' picks S, the last letter of Lepus; CUT means shortened. As a whole the clue describes the thing: Lepus is Latin for hare, and a hare's tail is short.
explanation.definitionFit: The short upright tail of a hare or rabbit has its own name, and Lepus is the hare genus.

clue.text: Be fully loaded as vessel such as schooner

definitions.text: Be fully loaded as vessel such as schooner

parts.words: Be fully loaded as vessel such as schooner
parts.note: a schooner is a sailing ship but also a large sherry or beer glass, and a full glass is filled to its top edge

explanation.definitionFit: A glass filled right to the top edge is said to be full to that edge, and the verb means to be full.

clue.text: Giving insincere speech, and bestowing kisses, perhaps?

explanation.definitionFit: Insincere support given in words only is the idiom; kissing is literally a service done with the mouth.

clue.text: Normal difficulty I identify between unknowns in puzzling fashion

parts.note: par is the normal standard, as in golf
ado is fuss or trouble

indicators.note: between means the letters go inside the pair given by unknowns

parts.note: x and y are the unknowns of algebra
to call someone something is to name or identify them

explanation.surface: Solving an equation, a normal difficulty is pinning down a value sitting between two unknowns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'between' puts I and CALL inside X and Y, the algebraic unknowns, giving XICALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done in a self-contradictory, baffling way is done in a puzzling fashion.

clue.text: With wild animals around, is unable to show bottle

indicators.note: around means the animals' word wraps round the inability word

parts.note: deer are wild animals
can't means is unable

explanation.surface: Surrounded by wild beasts, someone is unable to show courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts DEER round CANT. 'bottle' looks like British slang for nerve (courage), but here it is the glass container.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoppered glass vessel for serving wine or port is a type of bottle.

clue.text: Help for student joining one academic stream?

parts.note: a grant is money given to support a student
a means one

explanation.surface: A student loan or bursary makes it easier to enter higher education.
explanation.walkthrough: The GRANTA is the river through Cambridge, hence an 'academic stream'; the question mark flags the river sense of 'stream'.
explanation.definitionFit: The river flowing past Cambridge colleges is a watercourse with university associations.

clue.text: Stop with successful spell on the cards?

parts.note: a pack is a full set of playing cards
to be up is to be winning or ahead during a spell of play

explanation.surface: A card player quits while on a winning streak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' sets UP after PACK. To pack up is to stop work, or to break down.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish or quit an activity, packing away one's things, is to cease or halt.

clue.text: Debris I trusted could be disposed of

indicators.note: disposed means arranged, so the letters of I trusted are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Rubbish a person relied on could be thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be disposed of' rearranges I TRUSTED; 'disposed' means arranged, not thrown away.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose fragments and waste left behind are rubble or debris.

clue.text: Worthless as book, lacking clearly defined characters?

explanation.definitionFit: A book too dull to get through is unreadable; handwriting whose letters cannot be made out is illegible.

clue.text: I ask probing questions, angry with cut, backing underground worker

parts.note: cross means angry

indicators.note: backing means the word for cut is read from the end

parts.note: to axe is to cut
a miner works underground

explanation.surface: A furious, slashed coal miner demands answers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns AXE into EXA, which sits between CROSS and MINER.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawyer who questions the other side's witness in court asks searching questions, and speaks here in the first person.

clue.text: Hard to figure count losing head, in love with queen

indicators.note: in means the beheaded count sits inside the pair of letters
with joins the zero letter to the queen's letter

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O
R is regina, queen

indicators.note: losing head means the count's name drops its first letter

parts.note: Count Dracula is the vampire of Bram Stoker's novel

explanation.surface: A count missing his head, smitten with a queen, is difficult to understand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' cuts DRACULA to RACULA; 'in' puts it between O and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Like the pronouncements of an ancient oracle, it is cryptic and ambiguous, so hard to work out.

clue.text: Dickensian character in B crew I am reforming

indicators.note: reforming means forming again, so the letters of B crew I am are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Dickens figure turns up among a reorganised crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reforming' rearranges B CREW I AM. Mr Micawber is the hopeful debtor in David Copperfield.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilkins Micawber is a figure in David Copperfield, a novel by Dickens.

clue.text: Short of a rook — can unfinished game get replayed? can't wait until single clues

parts.note: R is the chess abbreviation for rook

indicators.note: get replayed means the pieces are played again in a new arrangement
unfinished means the word game loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A chess game without a rook is unfinished; can it be played again?
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' trims GAME to GAM; 'get replayed' rearranges A, R, CAN and GAM. A short is a measure of spirits, here a French brandy.
explanation.definitionFit: A brandy from Gascony is a spirit served as a small measure, so a drink of the strong kind.

clue.text: Cipher presents problem in murder investigation

explanation.definitionFit: A cipher is an insignificant person; detectives without a corpse have a major problem.

clue.text: Like some music from Bach or Albinoni

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the composers' names as they stand

explanation.surface: Some pieces by Bach or Albinoni are written for singers.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across baCH OR ALbinoni.
explanation.definitionFit: Music written for a choir is sung by many voices together.

clue.text: Brought in by boss if you become inflexible?

indicators.note: brought in by means the letters sit inside the words boss if you

explanation.surface: A boss might make you rigid.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across bOSS IF You. The question mark marks the sense of turning to bone, used of hardened attitudes.
explanation.definitionFit: To harden into bone, figuratively, is to grow rigid and stop changing.

clue.text: Hitch in public transport going round peripheral area

indicators.note: going round means the whole assembled bus-and-hitch is turned back to front
in means the hitch word goes inside the transport word

parts.note: a bus is public transport
rub is a hitch or snag, as in there's the rub

explanation.surface: A breakdown on the bus as it circles the outskirts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts RUB inside BUS to make BRUBUS; 'going round' turns the whole of it back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: A residential district on the edge of a town is an outlying, peripheral area.

clue.text: At the time of being about to succeed at university

indicators.note: to succeed means to follow, so the second piece comes after

parts.note: up means at university, as in up at Oxford
on means about, as in a book on birds

explanation.surface: Someone is close to doing well at university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to succeed' means come after: ON follows UP. 'Succeed' looks like doing well, but here it means follow.
explanation.definitionFit: As in 'on arrival', the word means at the moment of or immediately after.

clue.text: English want to stop strike in London area

indicators.note: to stop means the pieces fill a gap, plugging the strike word

parts.note: to lam is to beat or strike
to wish is to want

explanation.surface: The English desire to halt a walkout somewhere in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to stop' puts E and WISH inside LAM. 'strike' looks like industrial action, but LAM is an old word for thrash. LEWISHAM is a borough in south-east London.
explanation.definitionFit: A borough in south-east London is a district of the capital.

clue.text: Old author can only work with OED

indicators.note: work means the letters are worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: A dead writer can only get going with a big dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' rearranges CAN ONLY and OED; the author is Sir Arthur, creator of Sherlock Holmes.
explanation.definitionFit: The creator of Sherlock Holmes, who died in 1930, is a writer from the past.

clue.text: Charged with being drunk

explanation.definitionFit: A charged glass is filled to the top; someone drunk is said to be tanked or well-filled with drink.
